messages:
Alex (oncall): :rotating_light: Pager — multiple pods on node gpu-usw1-07 restarted, high ECC counts and node rebooted automatically. Notified by ops-bot at 14:00 UTC. Impact: a handful of customer requests 5xx, autoscale kicked in but tail latency spiked.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4421. Severity: P2. Pager targets: Alex, Joy. GCP case TODO. Logs collected to /incidents/1825300001/.
Alex (oncall): Quick snapshot: node reported KERNEL: 'NVRM: Xid 79' earlier, then ECC counters increased. Repro rate ~3 reboots in last 6 hours on that host pool. Putting link to Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/graphs/node/gpu-usw1-07
Sam (eng-runtime): On it. Can you paste node events and kube status? I want pod-level fallout and model fallbacks.
Eli (infra): grabbing gcloud and stackdriver logs now. Running: `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output gpu-usw1-07 --zone=us-west1-b --port=1-4`
Alex (oncall): Here are short outputs copied:
```
Node condition: KernelOOPS -> Reboot
Pods evicted: 42
OOM?: no
ECC counts (nvml): 0->124 in 2h
Temperature: node sensors show spike to 92C
```
Joy (sre): Thanks. Priority mitigation: cordon the node, drain gracefully, allocate pods to dedicated warm pool. Alex, can you cordon now? /cc @Maya for customer comms.
Alex (oncall): cordoned and drained. `kubectl cordon gpu-usw1-07; kubectl drain gpu-usw1-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
deploy-bot: Recent deploys: model-serving v2.16 rolled out 11h ago to pool-usw1. No immediate correlation but calling it out.
Maya (customer-success): FYI: one enterprise customer reported degraded throughput around 13:58 UTC, escalated to CS. I'll send interim note: we mitigated by moving work to other region. Will follow up with RCA.
Sam (eng-runtime): Pasting model-serving logs from one restarted pod:
```
2026-03-15T13:57:58Z ERROR model-server: failed to allocate GPU memory
2026-03-15T13:58:01Z WARN nvml: ECC/Corrected error count increased
2026-03-15T13:58:05Z INFO kernel: nv-peer memory event
```
Eli (infra): GCP console metrics show elevated PCIe AER events and thermal warnings coincident with ECC increase. Export snippet:
```
metric: compute.googleapis.com/guest/kernel_message
14:57:54 WARNING: PCIe AER: Corrected error, device 0000:3b:00.0
14:58:03 WARNING: NVML: ECC 0->124 corrected
14:58:33 CRITICAL: thermal_zone0 temp=92C
```
Joy (sre): Hypothesis list (we'll track inline):
1) Thermal overheating on host -> GPU ECC increase -> kernel triggers watchdog -> node reboot.
2) PCIe transient errors caused by host firmware bug -> memory corruption -> NV driver reboot.
3) Noisy neighbor VM saturating PCIe lanes causing AER and ECC cascades.
We should triage and eliminate sequentially.
Alex (oncall): I'm tagging hypothesis 1 highest because temperature spikes line up with reboots. Hypothesis 3 plausible because noisy neighbor has caused issues before in this pool.
Sam (eng-runtime): Can someone run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER` from the instance serial or ssh if available? Also check `dmesg | grep -i aer` and `journalctl -k`.
Eli (infra): Serial output includes kernel trace near reboot, pasting excerpt:
```
[   87.123456] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Uncorrected error messages
[   87.123789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid: 401
[   87.124000] kernel: watchdog: GPU reset failed
[   87.124210] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal GPU error
```
Sam (eng-runtime): That kernel panic line is new — suggests driver/kernel interplay. Also NVML ECC increases before panic, consistent with HW error escalation.
Maya (customer-success): Customer asks whether this was caused by workload — they run mixed batch and low-latency inference. They want timeline and mitigations.
Joy (sre): For customer comms: mitigating action: moved affected customers to other pool, increased fallback model concurrency, configured request queueing to smooth bursts. Noted in incident ticket.
Alex (oncall): I opened a GCP support case: case 987654321 — shared serial logs and NVML dumps. gcp-support-bot will post updates.
gcp-support-bot: Case 987654321 created. Assigned to support engineer. Preliminary note: investigating thermal telemetry and AER counts.
Eli (infra): Running `gcloud compute instances describe gpu-usw1-07 --zone=us-west1-b --format=json` to capture machine config; also requesting host maintenance logs from provider.
Sam (eng-runtime): Let's also check runtime config: were there any aggressive overcommit/auto-swap settings? `cat /etc/redwood/runtime.conf` (pasted): `gpu.power.limit=300W; kvcache.size=2G; prefetch=enabled` — nothing obviously risky.
Alex (oncall): Timeline so far (UTC):
- 13:56:22 first corrected ECC detected on node
- 13:57:10 AER events start
- 13:58:03 NVML ECC corrected error count jumps
- 13:58:33 thermal sensor spikes to 92C
- 13:58:45 kernel panic and node reboot
- 13:59:12 autoscaler reschedules pods
- 14:03:00 node comes back, kubelet restarts pods
- 14:10:00 second smaller ECC burst but no reboot (node later cordoned)
Alex (oncall): I also uploaded NVML dumps to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/1825300001/nvml-dump.tar.gz
Sam (eng-runtime): Action item: reproduce ECC spike on a spare host by running stress-ng + GPU workload in isolation? We should be careful; coordinate with infra.
Eli (infra): I spun up a repro instance in a different host group with the same image. Running synthetic workload to see if temperature ramps the same. Early signs: temperature climbs but not to 92C under same wall-time.
Joy (sre): Adding mitigations executed in-thread:
- Node cordoned and drained (Alex) :white_check_mark:
- Workloads moved to warm pool :white_check_mark:
- Customer throttles/queueing applied :white_check_mark:
- Support case filed to GCP :white_check_mark:
- Probe instance created for repro :in_progress:
Sam (eng-runtime): One more data point: NV driver revision on node is 535.54; known issues reported in vendor changelog for PCIe AER handling on that revision. Filing bug link: https://nvvendor.com/bugs/535-aer
Eli (infra): Provider responded: host-level firmware update pending for this rack; they observed other customers with corrected ECC on neighbor hosts. They flagged noisy neighbor but not confirmed. GCP advises to keep host offline pending firmware patch.
gcp-support-bot: Update on case 987654321: Provider identified rack-level thermal sensor threshold miscalibration and scheduled firmware roll for 2026-03-16 02:00 UTC. Recommended to keep node cordoned.
Maya (customer-success): I'll send follow-up to impacted customers: short summary + mitigation + ETA for RCA. Asking for one-sentence impact window to include in note.
Alex (oncall): Impact window (best estimate): 13:56–14:10 UTC for initial customer-visible errors; residual risk until host firmware patch. Will include in CS note.
Joy (sre): Owner assignments for RCA:
- Logs & timeline: Alex
- Kernel/NV driver analysis: Sam
- Cloud infra & provider liaison: Eli
- Customer comms: Maya
- Postmortem writeup: Joy
Action: schedule RCA review tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Any objections?
Sam (eng-runtime): No objections. I'll dig into driver tracepoints and kernel oops symbolicated.
Eli (infra): I'll follow up with provider for firmware rollout confirmation and request host replacement if recurrence after patch.
Alex (oncall): Closing the live mitigation phase — node remains cordoned. Will convert incident to postmortem after RCA meeting. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Noted: rollback not required. No further deploys to affected pool until patch confirmed.
gcp-support-bot: Case 987654321 status: awaiting provider firmware rollout. Will update post-deployment tests.
Joy (sre): If anyone finds contradictory evidence that points to noisy-VM rather than firmware/thermal, flag it here. For now we mark primary cause as 'provider thermal/firmware' pending kernel/drivers deep dive. :memo:
Alex (oncall): End of thread for live mitigation. Will append additional artifacts to the incident bucket as they arrive.
